regions.merged_text: My dear Brother Edward. Rt. Rev. Monsignore: God bless you these days of grace. I started Monday with the intention of writing you a letter as I hoped would be worthwhile. I have not been able to finish it and my answer to your proposition about the Gregorian Masses ought to be already on the way thither. In a way I regret I'll have to be a disappointment in this really generous proposition You will understand from the fact that as members of the Order we have as a rule only the disposal of two holy Mass intentions per month. Otherwise all intentions for holy Masses are life (left) to the disposal and appointment of the local Superior. I have enrolled poor, dear Grace, however, anumber of times in the Seraphic Mass -Association, which in my conviction, means, each time an emmense benefit. In fact, judging from the reports of favors as received there therefrem, it is not easy to find a comparason. Deo gratias! Some how I did not receive word of Grace's death till after my High-Mass on Sunday April 12. Some one phoned about it while I was on the Altar saying they would call later and that was the end of it. Brother Porter was not particular about the name of the caller but Thomas Brady wired that evening. Luckyly someone had sent in a request for a special holy Mass for Fr. Sol's Intent., and the following day I had a regular Missam propriam. I was happy to offer them both for poor, dear, Grace Agatha R. I. P. After all, how can we ever be grateful as we ought to be, for another so hopeful and beautiful death added to the happy list so far without exception. Glory and thanks be to God! Re - quiescant I.P. It would just seem that dear Mother and Father are keeping up their happy old night-prayers for -- "and for a happy death and a favorable judgement." I hope we all -- still left behind in this exile -- keep up on our part too that beautiful so beautiful feature of Communion of Saints. God bless you again Father - -
